title: Migrate Hyprland config from hyprlang (.conf) to Lua
description:
Hyprland deprecated the hyprlang (.conf) config format in 0.55; 0.56/0.57 print a
deprecation warning ("you are using the conf config support, deprecated"). New format
is Lua. We're on 0.56.1.

DECISION (2026-08): ignore for now. .conf still works fully in 0.56.x and upstream says
it stays 1-2 more releases. This bead tracks the eventual migration, not urgent.

Current state:
- home-manager/desktop/hypr/default.nix sets configType = "hyprlang" and feeds a raw
  197-line hypr.conf via builtins.readFile into extraConfig, plus theme border overrides
  and an optionalString homework block (OBS scene binds, remarkable device rule).
- home-manager/desktop/hypr/hypr.conf is the hand-written config blob.

Migration when we do it:
- Set configType = "lua". Either port the config to home-manager settings = { ... }
  (module emits hl.() Lua calls) or write native hyprland.lua.
- KNOWN BUG: HM module emits invalid hl.exec-once() for exec-once; use the
  hl.on("hyprland.start", function() ... end) workaround (see HM issue #9341).
- Port theme col.active_border/col.inactive_border overrides and the optionalString
  config.custom.homework block (OBS scene binds F1-F3, remarkable device rule).
- Note: HM default configType flips to "lua" in a future release; keep explicit
  "hyprlang" until we migrate so nothing flips under us.

VERIFY: after switch, Hyprland starts with no deprecation warning, all binds/rules/theme
colors intact, homework OBS + remarkable rules still apply on that machine.

title: Migrate eduroam.env to sops-nix on framework
description:
Currently configuration.nix:17-18 loads eduroam WiFi (WPA-EAP) credentials via
networking.networkmanager.ensureProfiles.environmentFiles = ["/etc/nixos/secrets/eduroam.env"],
gated by lib.mkIf (builtins.pathExists ...). That file is gitignored (.gitignore:6,
"secrets/eduroam.env") and lives only as a raw unencrypted file on disk -- never committed,
never backed up, has to be manually recreated by hand on every reinstall. This is exactly the
problem sops-nix (added in nixos-sops-2u6) solves.

Catch: eduroam is used on the 'framework' machine (laptop), but sops-nix is currently wired up
ONLY for 'homework' (see machines/homework/configuration.nix -- imports
inputs.sops-nix.nixosModules.sops and sets sops.age.sshKeyPaths =
["/etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key"]; no sops.secrets are declared anywhere yet). 'framework' has
its own config at machines/framework/configuration.nix (currently: { config, lib, pkgs,
userName, ... }: { imports = [ ./hardware-configuration.nix ]; ... }, no inputs arg).

Steps:
1. In machines/framework/configuration.nix: add `inputs` to the function's arg set, add
   `inputs.sops-nix.nixosModules.sops` to imports, and set
   `sops.age.sshKeyPaths = ["/etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key"];` (mirrors
   machines/homework/configuration.nix -- framework has its own ssh host key at
   /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key, so this reuses the same no-separate-key-to-generate pattern).
2. Derive framework's age public key: `nix run nixpkgs#ssh-to-age -- -i
   /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub` (run ON the framework machine, not homework -- different
   host key).
3. Add that recipient to .sops.yaml under a new anchor (e.g. &framework), and reference it in
   the creation_rules for the new secrets/eduroam.yaml file (keep homework's existing
   &homework anchor/rule untouched; framework needs its own rule since the two machines don't
   share a decryption key).
4. Create secrets/eduroam.yaml (structure: `eduroam.env: |` followed by the raw
   EAP_IDENTITY=...\nEAP_PASSWORD=... contents, or whatever keys NetworkManager's
   environmentFiles expects -- check the current /etc/nixos/secrets/eduroam.env by hand on
   framework for the exact key names before writing this, since that file is gitignored and
   not visible from other machines). Encrypt with
   `nix run nixpkgs#sops -- --encrypt --in-place secrets/eduroam.yaml`.
5. Declare `sops.secrets."eduroam/env" = { sopsFile = ../../secrets/eduroam.yaml; };` in
   machines/framework/configuration.nix.
6. Update configuration.nix:17-18 to use
   `environmentFiles = [ config.sops.secrets."eduroam/env".path ];` instead of the
   pathExists-gated raw file path (drop the `lib.mkIf (builtins.pathExists ...)` guard
   entirely once the secret is sops-managed -- it'll always exist after activation).
7. Update docs/secrets.md's "Adding a secret for a new service" section if the recipe needs
   adjusting for the multi-machine-recipient case (each machine gets its own age key + its own
   creation_rule + sopsFile, since keys aren't shared across machines).

Acceptance: `nix build .#nixosConfigurations.framework.config.system.build.toplevel` succeeds;
after deploy on framework, eduroam still connects; the raw secrets/eduroam.env file (and its
.gitignore entry) can be deleted once migrated.

title: Pins the eduroam RADIUS server name so a rogue AP cannot harvest the MSCHAPv2 credential
Enable native services.linkding on homework (127.0.0.1:9090)
description:
Enable the native nixpkgs linkding module on homework. Depends on sops.

Facts: nixpkgs ships services.linkding (nixos/modules/services/web-apps/linkding.nix). Defaults: address=127.0.0.1, port=9090, dataDir=/var/lib/linkding, sqlite backend, environmentFile option, settings attrset for LD_* vars, openFirewall=false.

Steps (edit /etc/nixos/machines/homework/configuration.nix):
1. services.linkding = { enable = true; address = "127.0.0.1"; port = 9090; environmentFile = config.sops.secrets."erwin-linkding/linkding-env".path; }. Keep openFirewall=false -- the UI is reached over tailscale (services.tailscale.enable is already true globally), never the public internet.
2. environmentFile supplies LD_SUPERUSER_NAME / LD_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD (from sops) so the admin user is auto-created on first start.
3. If any hardening override is needed, follow the services.ollama pattern (systemd.services.linkding.serviceConfig = { ... }) rather than editing the module.
4. After first deploy, log into the UI over tailscale, create an API token, and record it into the sops TARGET_TOKEN secret (closes the loop with the drainer).

Acceptance: after `just deploy` (nixos-rebuild --flake .#loxnix), linkding answers on 127.0.0.1:9090 over tailscale; `journalctl -u linkding` clean; admin login works; firewall still shows only mosh UDP open.

title: Add sops-managed Tailscale authkey for unattended join
description:
Right now every machine (configuration.nix:150, services.tailscale.enable = true;) requires
an interactive 'sudo tailscale up' after each deploy/reinstall to join the tailnet (see
comment at configuration.nix:149). homework in particular is meant to be an always-on
headless server (see machines/homework/configuration.nix comments about it being SSH'd into
for long tasks) -- a fresh install or a tailscale state wipe currently can't rejoin without
physical/interactive access.

sops-nix is already wired up for homework (machines/homework/configuration.nix imports
inputs.sops-nix.nixosModules.sops, sets sops.age.sshKeyPaths =
["/etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key"]; no secrets declared yet -- this would be the first).

Steps:
1. Generate a Tailscale auth key from the admin console
   (https://login.tailscale.com/admin/settings/keys) -- prefer a reusable, tagged key scoped
   to this device if the tailnet uses ACL tags, with a sane expiry (or reusable + ephemeral
   off, so re-running doesn't spawn duplicate nodes).
2. Create secrets/tailscale.yaml with a single key, e.g.:
   ```
   tailscale:
     authkey: |
       tskey-auth-...
   ```
   Encrypt with `nix run nixpkgs#sops -- --encrypt --in-place secrets/tailscale.yaml` (matches
   the existing secrets/*.yaml creation_rule in .sops.yaml for homework's recipient).
3. In machines/homework/configuration.nix declare:
   `sops.secrets."tailscale/authkey" = { sopsFile = ../../secrets/tailscale.yaml; };`
4. Set, on homework specifically:
   `services.tailscale.authKeyFile = config.sops.secrets."tailscale/authkey".path;`
   (`config` is already in scope in machines/homework/configuration.nix). Check the
   services.tailscale module option shape in nixpkgs
   (nixos/modules/services/networking/tailscale.nix) before writing this -- confirm
   authKeyFile vs a systemd-tailscale-autoconnect service pattern is the current recommended
   approach in the nixpkgs version this flake pins.
5. Leave framework/dellxps on the manual `tailscale up` flow for now (they're not the
   always-on headless case) unless the user wants this everywhere.

Acceptance: after a fresh `nixos-rebuild switch` on homework with tailscale state cleared (or
a real reinstall), the box appears in the tailnet without any interactive `tailscale up` step.

title: Declare erwin-linkding + linkding secrets in sops (infra already wired)
description:
Declare the erwin-linkding + linkding secrets in sops. The sops-nix INFRASTRUCTURE is already in place — do NOT redo it:
 - flake input exists (flake.nix:53-55, github:Mic92/sops-nix)
 - homework imports the module and derives its age key from the ssh host key (machines/homework/configuration.nix:11,19: inputs.sops-nix.nixosModules.sops + sops.age.sshKeyPaths)
 - .sops.yaml exists with homeworks recipient (age1epky306e...) and a creation_rule for secrets/*.yaml
 - docs/secrets.md documents the flow

REMAINING WORK (none of this exists yet — there is no secrets/ dir and no sops.secrets declared anywhere):
1. Create secrets/erwin-linkding.yaml (sops-encrypted, encrypt with `nix run nixpkgs#sops -- --encrypt --in-place secrets/erwin-linkding.yaml`) containing:
   - drainer env: DRAIN_SECRET and TARGET_TOKEN (local linkding API token). DRAIN_SECRET must equal the value set in the Netlify dashboard. TARGET_TOKEN is filled after first linkding login (see lkd).
   - linkding superuser bootstrap: LD_SUPERUSER_NAME, LD_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD.
2. Declare sops.secrets.* (with owner/mode, sopsFile = ../../secrets/erwin-linkding.yaml) in machines/homework/configuration.nix so the linkding service and the drainer service can each read their env file.

Follow the upstream-module + `systemd.services.<name>.serviceConfig` override pattern already used for services.ollama.

Acceptance: `nixos-rebuild build --flake /etc/nixos#homework` succeeds; secrets decrypt to /run at activation; ciphertext safe to commit.

title: Authorizes an ed25519 SSH key in place of the legacy RSA one
description:
PROBLEM
machines/base.nix line 32 authorizes a single ssh-rsa public key for the primary user. Committing
a public key is correct and the file already documents why it is safe. The issue is the algorithm:
RSA with SHA-1 signatures (ssh-rsa) is deprecated, OpenSSH disables it by default from 8.8
onward, and the key predates the current setup. ed25519 is smaller, faster, and has no
SHA-1 legacy.

FIX
1. On each device you connect FROM, generate `ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "<device>@<host>"` if one
   does not already exist.
2. Add the resulting public key(s) to the `openssh.authorizedKeys.keys` list in
   machines/base.nix, keeping the RSA key alongside them for now.
3. Deploy, then verify remote login works with the new key: `ssh -i ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 -o
   IdentitiesOnly=yes lox@homework.ohrg.org`.
4. Only once that is confirmed from every device you use, remove the ssh-rsa entry.

Do not remove the RSA key before step 3 succeeds — password authentication is disabled, so a
mistake here locks you out of the remote machine.

ACCEPTANCE
- machines/base.nix authorizes at least one ssh-ed25519 key.
- Remote login verified with the ed25519 key.
- The ssh-rsa entry is gone (or a follow-up note records which device still needs migrating).
